sections.synopsis: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.

A shallow intrusion of magma occurred overnight within the summit region near the existing eruption location. North and south vent continue to have intermittent overflows, spatter, and strong glow. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.
A shallow intrusion of magma is occurring within the summit region near the existing eruption location in Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park.

Intermittent overflows and spatter from both north and south vents occurred over the past day Halema'uma'u crater at the summit of Kīlauea. West vent had occasional glow overnight. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

Numerous rapid cycles of south vent overflows and drainback occurred overnight within Halema'uma'u crater at the summit of Kīlauea. The north and south vents had strong glow and intermittent spatter. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

The Halemaʻumaʻu eruption of Kīlauea volcano is currently erupting small overflows from both the north and south vents. It is not possible to forecast the onset of episode 55 fountains or if they will occur.

The Halemaʻumaʻu eruption of Kīlauea volcano is currently erupting small overflows from both the north and south vents. It is not possible to forecast the onset of episode 55 fountains or if they will occur.

Small overflows from the north vent continue within Halema'uma'u crater at the summit of Kīlauea. All vents have strong glow and intermittent spatter. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

Small overflows from the north vent continue, along with tiny overflows from the south vent starting overnight. All vents have strong glow and intermittent spatter. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

Small overflows from the north vent continue for the fourth day. All vents have strong glow, with overflows and intermittent spatter from the north vent. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

Precursory overflows from the north vent continue for the third day. All vents have strong glow, with overflows and intermittent spatter from the north vent. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

Precursory overflows from the north vent resumed on September 22. Strong glow from all vents continued with intermittent spatter from the north and south vents. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

Precursory overflows from the north vent resumed last night. Strong glow from all vents continued with intermittent spatter from the north and south vents. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

Eruption of precursory lava flows from the north vent of the of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption restarted around 10:10 p.m. HST on September 22, 2026. It is unclear if this activity will lead to a lava fountaining episode.

The north, south, and west vents continue to glow with minor intermittent spatter from the north and south vents. Minor summit inflation continued overnight. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.
The north, south, and west vents continue to glow with minor intermittent spatter from the north vent. Minor summit inflation occurred overnight. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.
The Halemaʻumaʻu eruption of Kīlauea volcano is currently paused, current forecast for episode XX fountaining onset is MONTH XX-XX.
The Halemaʻumaʻu eruption of Kīlauea volcano is currently paused, current forecast for episode XX fountaining onset is MONTH XX-XX.
The north, south, and west vents continue to glow and emit flames with minor intermittent spatter. Minor summit inflation occurred overnight. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

There is currently no active lava on the ground. The north and west vents continue to glow and emit flames. Minor summit inflation occurred overnight. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

There is currently no active lava on the ground. The north, south, and west vents continue to glow and emit flames, with minor intermittent spatter. Minor summit inflation occurred overnight. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.
Magnitude-4.1 earthquake near Pāhala, Island of Hawaiʻi

The new vents stagnated last night, there is currently no active lava on the ground. The north, south, and west vents continue to glow. A minor summit deflation began at about 5 pm HST last night. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

Five new vents have now opened on and near the northwest wall of Halemaʻumaʻu crater and produced small lava flows. Spattering continues from the north vent, periodic bursts from south and west vents. Summit inflation is stalled, tremor is increasing.

New vents opened at Kīlauea summit eruption site last night. Kīlauea summit region is pressurized above the level required to start a fountaining episode. Additional changes to the type of activity/eruption location could potentially occur.

Two new vents opened on and near the northwest wall of Halemaʻumaʻu crater last night and produced small lava flows. Spattering continues from the north vent with periodic bursts from south vent. Summit inflation stalled with opening of the new vents.

Kīlauea has been intermittently erupting bursts of spatter building a small cone around the north vent in Halemaʻumaʻu; no precursory flows since September 12. Summit inflation stalled last night further delaying the onset of episode 55 fountaining.

Kīlauea volcano is intermittently erupting short, precursory lava flows with 104 recorded since this activity began on September 7. The onset of episode 55 fountaining is likely today or tomorrow, if conditions remain favorable.
Magnitude-4.0 earthquake south of Pāhala, Island of Hawaiʻi. Light shaking reported, no damage expected.

Kīlauea volcano is intermittently erupting short, precursory lava flows with over 100 recorded since the activity that began September 7. The onset of episode 55 fountaining is likely today or tomorrow, if inflation patterns remain consistent.

Kīlauea volcano is intermittently erupting short, precursory lava flows continuing the activity that began September 7. Summit inflation returned last night. Episode 55 fountaining is likely today, September 11, if inflation patterns remain consistent.

Kīlauea volcano is intermittently erupting short, precursory lava flows continuing the activity that began September 7. The forecast window for onset of episode 55 fountaining is now September 10-11 given no change in summit inflation since yesterday.
Kīlauea volcano is erupting. Precursory overflows, which began on September 7, continued for the past 24 hours. A forecast window of September 9-10 is likely for the start of episode 55 fountaining.

Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. Precursory overflows started yesterday afternoon, but stopped overnight during summit deflation. A forecast window of September 8-10 is likely for the start of episode 55.
Precursory low-level eruptive activity before episode 55 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption began around 15:45 p.m. HST on September  7, 2026.
Precursory low-level eruptive activity before episode 55 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption began around 15:45 p.m. HST on September  7, 2026.

Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. The summit inflated rapidly during the past 24 hours but appears to be stalling this morning. A forecast window of September 7-10 is likely for the start of episode 55.

Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. The summit inflated rapidly during the past 24 hours after being stalled the previous day. A forecast window of September 7-10 is likely for the start of episode 55.

Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. Summit inflation remains stalled for the past 24 hours after a day of deflation. A forecast window of September 7-13 is likely for the next fountain episode.

Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. The summit is currently in a deflationary step since yesterday morning. A forecast window of September 7-13 is likely for the next fountain episode.

Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. Summit reinflation has continued over the past day. A forecast window of September 7-12 is likely for the next fountain episode.
